sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Israeli Settlers Attack European Diplomats in West Bank
cards.content: A delegation of European diplomats from Belgium, France, Poland, and the Catholic Church was attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. The Belgian government condemned the assault, calling for Israel to bring those responsible to justice. France also condemned the attack, urging Israel to halt the violence and ensure the safety of civilian populations. The US Secretary of State Marco Rubio separately condemned an attack on a Washington Post photographer, Heidi Levine, saying it was 'disturbing' and 'not a good look.' The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) are investigating the attacks, while the office of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu questioned the motives behind the incidents.

cards.title: UK woman detained for two months over sister's activism in Egypt
cards.content: Eman el-Shazly, a 46-year-old woman from Handsworth Wood, Birmingham, has been detained by Egyptian authorities for two months, allegedly due to her sister's online activism. Her husband, Zeesharn Moustapha, has called on Prime Minister Andy Burnham to intervene and help secure her release. Moustapha claims that their family has been left feeling helpless, with no contact with el-Shazly and her health deteriorating due to a lack of food and medical assistance. The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office has stated that it is in contact with Egyptian authorities, but Moustapha feels that their efforts are 'useless' with no progress made in securing el-Shazly's release. The situation has left Moustapha and their four children feeling distraught and unsure of what to do.

cards.title: Attack on St. Petersburg oil facilities kills one, injures five
cards.content: At least one person was killed and five others injured in an overnight attack on St. Petersburg, Russia, which targeted two oil facilities, a logistics centre, and a data centre. The attack also damaged 12 apartment buildings, two homes, and temporarily closed Pulkovo Airport. The city's governor said fires were being extinguished at the oil terminal and depot. Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities, but resumed them earlier this week. Russia's Defence Ministry reported shooting down over 1,000 Ukrainian drones overnight.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Texas A&M Study Finds Language, Reasoning Linked to Math Skills
cards.content: Researchers at Texas A&M University have found that language and reasoning skills are strong predictors of math performance. The study, published in the Journal of Intelligence, analyzed 122 test batteries and found that cognitive abilities such as number sense, fluid reasoning, and comprehension knowledge are essential for math learning. According to Dr. Daniel Hajovsky, the study's lead researcher, math requires students to recognize patterns, interpret information, and apply logical reasoning, drawing on a range of cognitive skills that also support learning in other subjects. The findings suggest that understanding what drives individual differences in mathematical ability can help educators identify learning needs early and provide targeted support. The study's conclusions may lead to new approaches to screening and instruction, potentially improving math outcomes for all students.

cards.title: NASA Backs Lunar Cave Search to Reveal Moon's Volcanic History
cards.content: NASA is backing a project to search for a hidden lunar cave, which could reveal how ancient volcanic activity shaped the Moon. The project, led by the Planetary Science Institute, will use a lander and rover to investigate a potential large cave near the Marius Hill Pit. The team will employ ground-penetrating radar, seismic sensors, and gravity measurements to gather data, and if successful, the discovery could provide insights into the Moon's volcanic history and potentially even shelter astronauts from radiation and extreme temperatures. The project is funded by NASA's Payloads and Research Investigations on the Surface of the Moon program and is expected to provide valuable information about the Moon's subsurface and geology.

cards.title: Ancient Insect Found with Bendy Straw Feeding Organ in Amber
cards.content: Researchers have discovered a 99-million-year-old insect, Cretodorus noonoo, that had an ancient adaptation of a flexible and durable feeding organ, resembling a bendy straw, which allowed it to feed on tree sap. The newly described species, found in Myanmar, had mouthparts nearly twice the length of its body and was preserved in amber. The unique feature of the insect's mouthparts was densely covered with crosswise folds, which likely allowed it to bend and flex without collapsing. This discovery provides a glimpse into the insect world during the age of dinosaurs, and suggests that ancient forests created ecological conditions and opportunities very different from those we know today.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Losartan Medication Activates Brown Fat for Better Cardiovascular Health
cards.content: A new study on a blood pressure medication, Losartan, reveals that it could have a second use in activating brown fat, a tissue that burns energy to produce heat and is linked to better cardiovascular health. The research, published in Nature, analyzed medical records and PET/CT scans of over 100,000 patients and found that patients taking Losartan were more likely to have brown fat detected on their scans. The study also found that Losartan directly increased metabolic activity in brown fat cells and had a positive effect on the body's energy-burning fat. This discovery could lead to future treatments for people with normal blood pressure, as well as potential benefits for cardiovascular health. Additionally, the study found that brown fat was associated with lower rates of anxiety and depression, and its activity was linked to several health indicators, including blood sugar regulation, blood fats, and heart function. The researchers noted that further study is needed to fully understand the connections between brown fat and these health outcomes.

cards.title: Experimental treatment shows promise against C. difficile
cards.content: Experimental treatment for C. difficile gut infections, which is caused by an imbalance in the gut's microbial community, has shown promise in early laboratory and mouse research. The treatment, argyrin B, specifically kills the C. difficile bacteria while sparing the rest of the gut microbiome. Researchers have found that argyrin B is highly effective against C. difficile infections, reducing the bacterial load in laboratory experiments and mouse models. The compound acts by targeting a specific antibacterial site in the C. difficile bacteria and has shown little to no effect on beneficial microorganisms in the digestive tract. This could lead to a treatment that reduces the risk of further microbiome disruption, infections, and relapses, and may provide an alternative to the current treatment, fecal microbiota transfer, which is complex and unpleasant for many patients.

cards.title: Fat Before Carbs Regulates Blood Sugar in Mice Study
cards.content: In a breakthrough study, researchers found that eating fat before carbohydrates can help regulate blood sugar levels by slowing down stomach emptying and reducing the initial spike. This effect was observed in mice and may be applicable to humans, offering a potential dietary strategy to manage post-meal blood sugar rises, an important treatment target in diabetes.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: NASA data shows Arctic sea ice decline, threatening ice-free summers
cards.content: NASA's satellite data reveals a concerning decline in Arctic sea ice, with a possibility of nearly ice-free summers before 2050. The data shows a decrease in sea ice coverage during both winter and summer, with a significant decline in the thickness and age of the remaining ice. While there have been fluctuations in ice coverage over the years, the long-term trend suggests a persistent decline attributed to a combination of natural climate patterns and increasing global temperatures. The NASA data provides an uninterrupted record of Arctic sea ice growth and retreat since 1978, allowing scientists to track changes across nearly five decades.

cards.title: Avalanche Sweeps Away Over 100 Sheep in Himachal Pradesh
cards.content: In October 2025, Joginder Chand, a 50-year-old shepherd from Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district, set out to migrate his 600 sheep and goats to warmer grazing grounds in Kangra district. Suddenly, an avalanche swept away over 100 animals.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: The Howlers' album 'Heavy' tops charts with Portsmouth nods
cards.content: The British band, The Howlers, has achieved significant success with their new album 'Heavy', which features nods to their hometown, Portsmouth. The album reached the top 10 in several Official Charts, including album downloads, independent album breakers, and independent album charts. Guitarist and singer Adam Young credits the band's hard work and the album's authenticity for its success. Young notes that the album includes several references to Portsmouth, such as the centre stickers on the records and the CD, which are meant to resemble dazzle paint on navy ships. This album is seen as a step up from their previous work and a more authentic representation of the band. The Howlers spent the summer touring Germany supporting Deep Purple and have seen the album already mean a lot to people.

cards.title: Paul Shipper: From Film Fan to Illustrator of Marvel and Star Wars
cards.content: Paul Shipper, a film fan-turned-illustrator, has come a long way from creating movie poster artwork for fun. He has worked on some of Hollywood's biggest franchises, including Marvel, Indiana Jones, and Star Wars. Shipper's passion for illustration started when he was a kid, inspired by the films of George Lucas and Steven Spielberg. He shared his designs online, which led to opportunities that once seemed like a dream. The illustrator has worked on various projects, including posters and artwork for blockbuster titles, and has maintained a consistent artistic style despite working across different projects. Shipper is now involved in a charity exhibition, AMPjam Presents: We've Been Framed, which brings together more than 60 artists from around the world to create original artworks inspired by films and television shows.

cards.title: Scottish Actor Hopes Fans Accept His Accent in Marvel Series
cards.content: Scottish actor Ruaridh Mollica, who plays Tommy Maximoff in the Marvel Cinematic Universe miniseries VisionQuest, hopes fans will accept his Scottish accent. He says speaking in his own accent helped him bring the character to life, and he's excited to be part of the show.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: UK's Strong Growth Data Amid Global Economic Uncertainty
cards.content: A global economic tug-of-war is underway, with crises from energy shock, trade conflict, and war holding back growth, while massive AI spending and resilience from smaller economies pull in the other direction. At IMF meetings in Bangkok, finance ministers highlighted the UK's strong growth data and its model pupil status, but uncertainty remains about the future direction of the economy.

cards.title: Tesla Unveils Electric Sports Car with Hover Capabilities
cards.content: Tesla unveiled a new electric sports car that can hover and turn in mid-air, but it's unclear when flying cars will become a reality. Other news includes Meta's trial over claims its platforms are addictive, a ban on under-16s using social media, and the release of Nintendo's Switch 2. SpaceX's Starship rocket exploded during a test, and the US president is considering selling his Tesla car. A digital detox expert shares tips to help you stop looking at your phone.

cards.title: Small businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence tools
cards.content: Small businesses are adopting AI tools for customer support, marketing, document processing and data analysis. Lower-cost AI services are making technologies that were previously available mainly to large companies more accessible to smaller firms.
